Data-labelling defect, not a verification failure: 16 of the 492 stored pointwise_witnesses in certificates/COUNTEREXAMPLE_CANDIDATES_n7_limit.jsonl are at an ILLEGAL point (q < 1, all at t = 100, plus one at t = 1000 for &F]VhW[rSp?). The file correctly sets 'legal': false on all 16 ... But 15 of them also carry 'agrees_with_conjecture': false (stable and positive, but illegal) and 1 carries 'agrees_with_conjecture': true (illegal and unstable). That field means nothing at an illegal point and could mislead a reader who skips 'legal'.

(b) My sympy cross-check treated a repeated root as undecided. 186 points have repeated eigenvalues off the imaginary axis, from twin structure. ... After the fix every point is decided by all three methods.

overall_verdict.detail: Four independent implementations (sympy Rational + Hurwitz; pure Fraction + Hurwitz with dual charpoly; pure Fraction + exact root counting by Routh/Cauchy-index/sympy isolation with no Hurwitz minors; Fraction structural + limit) each confirm 124/124: not complete bidirected, legal (q>1), x>0 strictly, all eigenvalues of -I+W in the open left half-plane. Zero undecided points, zero method disagreements, zero mismatches against stored x / charpoly / adjacency. Each graph confirmed at 4 to 6 distinct legal rational points.

things_the_human_must_know: 15 of 123 limit graphs have an ILLEGAL first stored witness (t=100, q<=1; file flags legal=false). &F]VhW[rSp? has two illegal leading witnesses (t=100 and t=1000); its first legal witness is t=10000. If the hand verification used pointwise_witnesses[0], those 15 graphs were hand-checked at non-CTLN points. They are still confirmed counterexamples at their later legal witnesses and in-cell points.
In the limit file, 'agrees_with_conjecture' is set on illegal points (15 false, 1 true) and is meaningless there; consider nulling it when legal=false.
The task text's decoder hint for Geneson's graph (node 0 -> 1,2,3,4) is wrong; correct is 1,2,4,5.

The conventions line 'I - W = -delta I + (1+delta) J - (eps+delta) A_sigma' only holds with A_sigma read as the transpose (A^T restricted to sigma), which is what ctln.py/symbolic.py implement; a notation point, not a bug.
